inputs.name: GET.params
inputs.description: The route parameters from the path: params.id is the report id (a UUID that reportState creates) and must be 1 to 100 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens (safeId); params.type is the asset folder, and only 'assets' is served; params.file is the registered evidence file name, which must be listed in that report's manifest and not marked missing. A value that fails these checks makes GET throw an HttpError.

inputs.name: GET.request
inputs.description: The Fetch Request of this call, of which only the Range header is read through request.headers.get('range'); a missing header returns the whole asset with status 200. A Range header of the form bytes=start-end, bytes=start- or bytes=-N returns 206 with that slice, and a malformed or unsatisfiable header returns 416 with an empty body.

outputs.name: GET
outputs.description: The Response that GET resolves to, built by mediaResponse inside reportFile: status 200 with the whole asset, 206 with the requested slice, or 416 with no body, each served inline with Content-Type from the file extension (application/octet-stream when unknown), Accept-Ranges: bytes, Cache-Control: no-store and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. The bytes come from R2 when a matching, non-missing evidence item records storage 'r2' or 'r2-evidence', and from the report's assets folder otherwise.

errors.name: HttpError 404
errors.description: The fallback for any failure that is not already an HTTP error: an invalid or unknown report id, a report that is unreadable or not owned by this site, an asset name with a path separator, a missing asset, a symlink or other non-regular file, a path outside its folder, or storage that is not configured or cannot be read. Its message is always 'Registered asset not found', and it is the only error this handler creates itself, because the other errors come from reportFile and are rethrown unchanged.

errors.name: HttpError 404: Not found
errors.description: Thrown with the message 'Not found' when the type segment is anything other than 'assets'. The check runs after the report has been loaded, so an unknown report id gets the fallback 404 first.

errors.name: HttpError 404: Evidence expired or unavailable
errors.description: Thrown with the message 'Evidence expired or unavailable' when the report's manifest has no evidence item with this file name. It is checked before any bytes are read.

errors.name: HttpError 410: Evidence expired or unavailable
errors.description: Thrown with the message 'Evidence expired or unavailable' when the manifest lists this file name but every matching item is marked missing, for example when seal() could not register the asset at finalization.
